cities.name: Kochi
cities.overview: Kochi has been a spice-trading port for centuries, shaped by Arab, Chinese, Portuguese, Dutch, British and Jewish communities. Its historic quarters of Fort Kochi and Mattancherry sit on a peninsula facing the Arabian Sea.
cities.history: An old port on the Malabar spice route that became the seat of the Kingdom of Cochin. The Portuguese, Dutch and British each held Fort Kochi in turn, and each left churches, warehouses and houses behind.

cities.name: Munnar
cities.overview: A hill station at around 1,600 metres in the Western Ghats, surrounded by rolling tea estates, misty peaks and spice plantations.

cities.name: Alappuzha
cities.overview: Alappuzha (Alleppey) sits at the heart of Kerala's backwaters, a network of canals, lagoons and rivers that runs parallel to the coast. It is the main starting point for houseboat cruises.

cities.name: Thekkady
cities.overview: A small town in the Cardamom Hills on the edge of Periyar Tiger Reserve, known for spice plantations and forest activities.

cities.name: Thiruvananthapuram
cities.overview: Kerala's capital is a green, low-rise city of temples, palaces and museums, close to the beaches of Kovalam and Varkala.
cities.history: Capital of the Travancore kingdom from 1795, under rulers who governed in the name of Padmanabha, the deity of its great temple. It became the state capital of Kerala in 1956.

cities.name: Varkala
cities.overview: A coastal town where red laterite cliffs drop to the sea, about 50 km north of Thiruvananthapuram.

cities.name: Wayanad
cities.overview: A highland district in northern Kerala of forests, coffee and spice plantations, waterfalls and ancient caves.

cities.name: Thrissur
cities.overview: Kerala's cultural capital, built around a hill and a great temple, and the home of the Pooram festival.

cities.name: Kozhikode
cities.overview: Old Calicut, one of the medieval world's great spice ports, known today for its food and its beaches.

cities.name: Kannur
cities.overview: A northern city of forts, looms and quiet beaches, and the best place to see the Theyyam ritual.

cities.name: Kollam
cities.overview: An ancient seaport on the Ashtamudi Lake, and the southern gateway to the backwaters.

cities.name: Palakkad
cities.overview: A green town of rice fields, set in the one big gap in the Western Ghats.

cities.name: Kottayam
cities.overview: A town of churches, rubber and backwaters, with Kumarakom close by.

cities.name: Idukki
cities.overview: A district of high hills and great dams, in the middle of Kerala's spice country.

cities.name: Sabarimala
cities.overview: A forested hill in Pathanamthitta district and home to one of India's largest annual pilgrimages.

cities.name: Kasaragod
cities.overview: The northernmost district of Kerala, with a fine coastal fort at Bekal.

places.name: Alappuzha Backwaters
places.shortDescription: Cruise Kerala's palm-fringed canals and Vembanad Lake on a traditional kettuvallam houseboat.
places.description: The backwaters around Alappuzha are best experienced from a houseboat, a converted rice barge with bedrooms, a deck and an onboard cook. Overnight cruises drift past paddy fields below water level, village churches and toddy shops, while shikara boats and canoes reach narrower canals. Choose a licensed operator; boats must moor at night.
places.history: Alappuzha hosts the Nehru Trophy Boat Race on Punnamada Lake every August, named after Jawaharlal Nehru, who watched a snake-boat race here in 1952.
places.bestTimeNote: September to March. Visit in August for the Nehru Trophy Boat Race.

entryFee.note: Houseboats are priced per night by size and season; shikara rides are priced per hour.

timings.hours: Houseboat check-in around noon; check-out the next morning

places.name: Eravikulam National Park
places.shortDescription: High grasslands near Munnar that protect the endangered Nilgiri tahr and bloom blue with Neelakurinji every 12 years.
places.description: Forest-department buses carry visitors from the Rajamalai entrance up into rolling grassland and shola forest, where Nilgiri tahr (a mountain goat found only in the Western Ghats) graze close to the road. Anamudi, the highest peak in South India at 2,695 m, rises inside the park. Once every twelve years the slopes turn blue with Neelakurinji flowers; the next bloom is expected around 2030.
places.history: Declared a sanctuary in 1975 to protect the Nilgiri tahr and upgraded to a national park in 1978.
places.bestTimeNote: September to January. The park usually closes in February and March for the tahr calving season.

entryFee.note: Entry includes the park bus; foreigners pay more. Book online at weekends.

places.name: Fort Kochi
places.shortDescription: A walkable colonial-era quarter of Chinese fishing nets, old churches, art cafés and the Paradesi Synagogue.
places.description: Start at the giant cantilevered Chinese fishing nets on the seafront at sunset, then walk to St Francis Church and the Santa Cruz Basilica. Nearby Mattancherry has the Dutch Palace with its mural-lined rooms and Jew Town, home to spice warehouses, antique shops and the Paradesi Synagogue. In season, the Kochi-Muziris Biennale turns warehouses across the area into art venues.
places.history: Vasco da Gama was first buried at St Francis Church, built by the Portuguese in 1503 and one of the oldest European churches in India. The Paradesi Synagogue dates from 1568. The Portuguese, Dutch and British each ruled the port in turn.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; the Biennale typically runs from December to April.

entryFee.note: Free to explore; the Dutch Palace and synagogue charge small fees and close on some days.

timings.hours: Open all day; most monuments about 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM

places.name: Periyar Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: Evergreen forest around an artificial lake, known for elephant herds, boat cruises and bamboo rafting.
places.description: A boat cruise on Periyar Lake is the easiest way to spot elephants, gaur and sambar coming down to drink. For a closer look, the forest department runs guided nature walks, bamboo rafting, border hikes and night patrols led by local tribal guides. Tigers live here but are rarely seen. Thekkady town has spice gardens, Kathakali shows and martial-arts (kalaripayattu) performances.
places.history: The lake was created in 1895 when the Mullaperiyar Dam was built across the Periyar River. The forest around it became a tiger reserve in 1978.
places.bestTimeNote: October to April; animals gather at the lake in the drier months.

entryFee.note: Entry, boat cruise and activity fees are separate; book through the official Periyar site.

timings.hours: Boat cruises from about 7:30 AM to 3:30 PM

places.name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
places.shortDescription: A Vishnu temple where the deity reclines on the serpent Anantha, and one of the richest temples in the world.
places.description: The temple's seven-storey gopuram overlooks a large tank in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram. Inside, the 18-foot image of Padmanabha (Vishnu reclining on the serpent Anantha) is viewed through three doors. Entry is only for Hindus, and a strict dress code applies: men wear a mundu or dhoti and no shirt; women wear a sari, or a mundu over other clothes. Dhotis can be hired at the entrance.
places.history: The temple's origins are ancient and it is mentioned in Tamil Sangam literature. The present structure was largely rebuilt by Maharaja Marthanda Varma of Travancore in the 18th century. In 2011, vaults in the temple were found to hold treasure worth billions of dollars.

entryFee.note: Free darshan; paid options for special darshan. Entry for Hindus only.

timings.hours: Early-morning and evening darshan slots; check the temple website

location.address: West Nada, Fort, East Fort, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695023

places.name: Varkala Cliff
places.shortDescription: Red laterite cliffs above a sweeping beach, with a clifftop path of cafés and yoga shalas.
places.description: Varkala is the only place in southern Kerala where cliffs meet the Arabian Sea. A footpath runs along the North Cliff past guesthouses, cafés and Ayurveda centres, with steps leading down to Papanasam Beach, where pilgrims perform rites for their ancestors. The sea can be rough, so swim only near lifeguards. Sunset from the cliff is the highlight of the day.
places.history: The 2,000-year-old Janardana Swamy Temple near the beach makes Varkala a pilgrimage town, and the cliffs are a protected geological monument.

location.address: North Cliff, Varkala, Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala 695141

places.name: Edakkal Caves
places.shortDescription: A hilltop rock shelter in Wayanad with prehistoric carvings of humans, animals and symbols.
places.description: The Edakkal 'caves' are a natural cleft formed where a huge boulder fell across a crack in Ambukuthi Mala. Reaching them means a steep walk of about a kilometre and some rocky steps, rewarded by walls covered in engraved figures and views over Wayanad. Visitor numbers are limited each day, so arrive early.
places.history: The carvings are among the oldest in South India; some are believed to be thousands of years old, and the site also has later inscriptions. They were brought to wider attention in 1890 by Fred Fawcett, a police superintendent.
places.bestTimeNote: October to May; the climb can be slippery and closed in heavy rain.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee; daily visitor cap.

location.address: Ambukuthi Mala, Ambalavayal, Wayanad district, Kerala 673593

places.name: Mattancherry Palace
places.shortDescription: The Dutch Palace in Kochi, with fine Kerala murals and portraits of the Rajas of Kochi.
places.description: From outside it looks plain, but upstairs are some of the best murals in Kerala, with scenes from the Ramayana covering whole walls.
places.history: Built by the Portuguese in the 16th century as a gift to the Raja of Kochi, and later renovated by the Dutch.

places.name: Paradesi Synagogue
places.shortDescription: A 1568 synagogue in Jew Town, the oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth.
places.description: A small, bright room with hand-painted Chinese floor tiles, Belgian glass chandeliers and a clock tower outside. The lane around it is full of antique shops.
places.history: Built in 1568 for the Paradesi, or foreign, Jews of Kochi.

places.name: St. Francis Church, Kochi
places.shortDescription: One of the oldest European churches in India, where Vasco da Gama was first buried.
places.description: A simple whitewashed church on a green in Fort Kochi. Vasco da Gama's gravestone remains inside, although his body was later taken to Portugal.
places.history: Originally built in 1503 by the Portuguese and later used by the Dutch and the British.

sources.title: Church of Saint Francis, Kochi – Wikipedia

places.name: Cherai Beach
places.shortDescription: A calm beach on Vypin Island, 25 km from downtown Kochi, with the backwaters just behind it.
places.description: A long, swimmable beach with paddy fields and backwaters only metres behind the sand. It's an easy day out from Kochi and much quieter than Fort Kochi's shore.

places.name: Hill Palace, Tripunithura
places.shortDescription: Kerala's largest archaeological museum, once the royal seat of the Rajas of Kochi.
places.description: A cluster of buildings on a hilltop at Tripunithura, with royal crowns, old coins and palanquins. There's also a small deer park on the grounds.
places.history: The royal administrative office and official home of the Kochi Rajas.

places.name: Anamudi
places.shortDescription: The highest peak in south India at 2,695 m, rising above Eravikulam National Park.
places.description: The summit lies inside Eravikulam, and treks need a forest permit, which isn't always given. You can see it clearly from the park's Rajamalai section and from the Munnar highway.
highlights: Highest peak south of the Himalayas

places.name: Mattupetty Dam
places.shortDescription: A concrete dam and lake in the tea hills above Munnar, with boating and elephants nearby.
places.description: A popular stop on the drive to Top Station, with speed boats on the reservoir, a dairy farm nearby and elephants sometimes grazing along the banks.

places.name: Idukki Dam
places.shortDescription: A double-curvature arch dam on the Periyar, set in a narrow gorge between two granite hills.
places.description: A dramatic arch of concrete wedged between the Kuravan and Kurathi hills. It's among Asia's highest arch dams, and access for visitors is restricted to certain periods.

places.name: Vagamon
places.shortDescription: A hill station of tea, pine forest and rolling meadows, and a growing paragliding destination.
places.description: Grassy hills, tea gardens and a pine forest draw people here as a quieter alternative to Munnar. The Kerala International Paragliding Festival is held in these hills.

places.name: Kovalam
places.shortDescription: Kerala's most famous beach, a set of crescent bays 12 km from Thiruvananthapuram.
places.description: Three bays lie side by side beneath a red and white lighthouse, with restaurants and ayurvedic resorts crowded around them. Lighthouse Beach is the busiest.

places.name: Napier Museum
places.shortDescription: An art and natural history museum in a striking 19th-century Indo-Saracenic building.
places.description: Its striped brick building with Kerala-style roofs is a landmark of the city, and bronzes, carvings and old temple art fill the halls. The city zoo shares the grounds.
places.history: The museum grounds also house the Thiruvananthapuram Zoo, established in 1857.

places.name: Kuthiramalika
places.shortDescription: The Mansion of Horses: a Travancore palace with 122 carved wooden horses under its eaves.
places.description: A fine example of Kerala's wooden architecture, built close to the Padmanabhaswamy Temple. It's now a small museum with ivory thrones and Kathakali figures.
places.history: Built by the poet king Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma.

places.name: Ponmudi
places.shortDescription: A hill station 53 km from Thiruvananthapuram, with hairpin bends, tea and clouds at the top.
places.description: The road climbs through forest and 22 hairpin bends to green hills, tea estates and a deer park. It's an easy day out from the capital.

places.name: Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A sanctuary in the Western Ghats around the Neyyar Dam, with boating and a crocodile centre.
places.description: Lying where the Western Ghats meet the far south, it has a reservoir, a crocodile centre and the great rocky peak of Agasthyakoodam in the distance.

places.name: Vadakkunnathan Temple
places.shortDescription: An ancient Shiva temple in the heart of Thrissur, a classic of Kerala temple style and home of Pooram.
places.description: Tiled roofs, wooden galleries and Mahabharata murals inside a huge walled compound. The grounds around it host the Thrissur Pooram, Kerala's biggest festival.
places.bestTimeNote: Thrissur Pooram falls in the Malayalam month of Medam, usually in April or May.
highlights: Thrissur Pooram in April or May

places.name: Athirappilly Falls
places.shortDescription: Kerala's largest waterfall, on the Chalakudy River at the edge of the Sholayar forest.
places.description: A wide, thundering curtain of water, sometimes called the Niagara of India, that's reached on a short forest walk. It's at its fullest during the monsoon, and the road is lined with trees and hornbills.

places.name: Vazhachal Falls
places.shortDescription: A gentler waterfall 5 km above Athirappilly, in thick evergreen forest.
places.description: The Chalakudy River breaks up over wide rock shelves here, in forest that's among the richest in Kerala. The road on toward Valparai is a beautiful drive.

places.name: Guruvayur Temple
places.shortDescription: One of Kerala's most important Krishna temples, about 26 km from Thrissur.
places.description: A very busy temple, with a large number of weddings performed outside each morning. Only Hindus may enter, and the temple has an elephant sanctuary at Punnathur Kotta.

places.name: Kumarakom
places.shortDescription: A backwater village on Vembanad Lake, known for its houseboats and a bird sanctuary.
places.description: Coconut groves, paddy fields and canals on the largest lake in Kerala, with quieter water than Alappuzha. In 2023 The New York Times singled it out for its backwater tourism.

places.name: Ashtamudi Lake
places.shortDescription: A palm-shaped lake with eight arms at Kollam, the gateway to the backwaters.
places.description: A huge wetland of many arms, with Chinese fishing nets and coconut-fringed islands, including Munroe Island. The boat trip from Kollam to Alappuzha starts here.
places.history: Ashtamudi means eight-braided, after the lake's many arms.

places.name: Jatayu Earth's Center
places.shortDescription: A huge bird sculpture on a rock at Chadayamangalam, in a 350 m high hilltop nature park.
places.description: A giant sculpture of the mythical bird Jatayu lies across a hilltop, reached by cable car. There's an adventure park at the same site, and the views stretch across the green countryside.

sources.title: Jatayu Earth's Center Nature Park – Wikipedia

places.name: Sabarimala Temple
places.shortDescription: A major Ayyappa pilgrimage site in the Pathanamthitta forest, which draws millions every year.
places.description: Pilgrims in black walk through the forest to reach the hilltop shrine after weeks of fasting, climbing the holy 18 steps at the end. The site opens only during set seasons.
places.bestTimeNote: The main pilgrimage season runs from mid-November to mid-January. The temple is otherwise open only at set times.

places.name: Silent Valley National Park
places.shortDescription: A rainforest in the Nilgiri hills, saved from a dam by a famous 1970s public campaign.
places.description: Tall virgin rainforest, entered only with a forest department guide on a trip from Mukkali. It's a home of the lion-tailed macaque, among other rare species.
places.history: A long campaign in the 1970s stopped a planned hydroelectric dam here.

places.name: Palakkad Fort
places.shortDescription: A granite fort in the heart of Palakkad, built by Hyder Ali and well-preserved.
places.description: A compact, moated fort right in the town centre, with thick walls and a green maidan beside it. It's kept up by the Archaeological Survey of India.
places.history: Hyder Ali rebuilt it in 1766, and it later fell to the British.

places.name: Malampuzha Dam
places.shortDescription: Kerala's largest reservoir, with gardens, a ropeway and a famous sculpture of a Yakshi.
places.description: A popular family outing with terraced gardens, a telescopic tower and a ropeway over the gardens. The big reclining Yakshi sculpture by Kanayi Kunhiraman is a landmark.
places.history: Built after Independence by the then Madras state.

places.name: Nelliyampathy
places.shortDescription: A hill station 60 km from Palakkad, with hairpin bends, orange orchards and tea estates.
places.description: A winding road passes Pothundi Dam and climbs to estates of tea, coffee and oranges. It's still a fairly quiet hill station, with viewpoints across the plains.

places.name: Banasura Sagar Dam
places.shortDescription: India's largest earth dam, with small islands in the reservoir and Banasura Hill behind it.
places.description: A huge earth embankment holding back a blue reservoir dotted with islands. Speedboats run from the dam, and treks go up the peak behind it.

places.name: Chembra Peak
places.shortDescription: The highest peak in Wayanad at 2,100 m, with a heart-shaped lake on the way up.
places.description: A popular day trek through grassland and tea to a small heart-shaped lake. Forest department guides are compulsory, and the route may shut in fire season.

places.name: Soochipara Falls
places.shortDescription: A three-tiered waterfall in the forest of Wayanad, known too as Sentinel Rock Waterfalls.
places.description: A short forest walk leads down to a big plunge pool below a cliff of tall rock. It's a popular swimming spot when the water's not too high.

places.name: Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: Kerala's second largest sanctuary, in four hill ranges, with elephants and tigers in tall forest.
places.description: Set where the Kerala hills meet Bandipur and Nagarhole, with jeep safaris at Muthanga and Tholpetty. Elephants are the star here.
places.history: Established in 1973, and part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

places.name: Thirunelli Temple
places.shortDescription: An ancient Vishnu temple on Brahmagiri hill, near the Karnataka border, in deep forest.
places.description: A granite temple in a green valley, reached along a forest road. Pilgrims come to perform last rites for ancestors at the Papanasini stream.

places.name: Kappad Beach
places.shortDescription: The beach near Kozhikode where a stone marks Vasco da Gama's arrival in 1498.
places.description: A rocky little beach, usually quiet, with a monument that recalls the Portuguese landing. It's a short drive from the city.
places.history: A monument records that Vasco da Gama landed here in 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India.

places.name: Beypore
places.shortDescription: A port town at the Chaliyar estuary, known for building traditional wooden Uru ships.
places.description: Master carpenters here still build huge wooden dhows by hand, as they've done for centuries for Arab traders. A long pier stretches out along the river mouth.

places.name: St. Angelo Fort
places.shortDescription: A sea-facing fort in Kannur, built by the Portuguese in 1505, with views of Mappila Bay.
places.description: Grey laterite walls looking out over the Arabian Sea, with cannons and bastions intact. It passed from the Portuguese to the Dutch and the British.
places.history: Built by the first Portuguese Viceroy of India, Dom Francisco de Almeida, in 1505.

places.name: Muzhappilangad Beach
places.shortDescription: A 4 km drive-in beach in Kannur district, with firm sand and rocks that break the waves.
places.description: One of the few beaches in India where you can legally drive on the sand. In 2016 the BBC named it one of the six best beaches in the world for driving.

places.name: Thalassery Fort
places.shortDescription: The British fort at Thalassery, a former European trading centre on the Malabar coast.
places.description: A square laterite fort with big doors and a lighthouse, standing on a low hill by the sea. Thalassery itself is known for its cakes, cricket and circus.
places.history: One of the most important European trading centres in Kerala in the 18th century.

places.name: Bekal Fort
places.shortDescription: A huge keyhole-shaped fort on the sea, built by Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi in 1650.
places.description: Kerala's largest fort, with a walkway around the ramparts right over the waves. The beach beside it is a good place for sunset.
places.history: Built by Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi in 1650.
